summary.scope: Four exact atan/asin-acos/commuted-atan/pi identities at four coefficient widths, cold and numerically warmed requests, three exact perturbations and four allowances. Each definitive sign agrees with the exact identity; unlimited retry certifies it and a later zero-budget query retains the proof. Python Fraction and Rug independently check each numerical observation against the exact rational perturbation. A finite public/serialized corpus, not an allocation/time proof.

New budgeted APIs on 48 symbolic angle fixtures with nine finite non-rational residuals, four trig families and serialized/public controls. Includes sqrt(2), ln(2), exp(1), atan(1/2), sqrt(2)-1, signed/scaled sqrt(2), and exp(100); lattice/non-lattice periodic coefficients, nearby poles, factored/distributed arithmetic, cancelled extreme offsets and 64 offset wrappers. Four-query schedule shares one allowance of one million work units. A prior zero-unit request is typed or reuses an already available constructor cache; a later zero-unit request must reuse the completed cache and retain every established sign. All returned samples are independently enclosed. Directed 1024-bit MPFR pi and residual enclosures feed exact derivative-one sin/cos intervals and exact quotient bounds. Each process is capped at 192 MiB, CPU 2/3 seconds and wall 4 seconds. Scoped evidence, not an exhaustive proof or matched benchmark.

24 exact principal-root product identities, including reciprocal forms and 64/256/1024-bit rational factors, three exact perturbations and four allowances. Numerical warmup precedes the explicit shared allowance. Independent rational oracles check both approximations; every definite sign must agree, and an unlimited retry must certify and retain the result at zero budget. This is a scoped accounting/certificate replay, not a wall-time or memory proof.

12 additional cube/fourth-root product identities with 64/256/1024-bit rational factors and reciprocal forms, three exact perturbations and four allowances. A 65536-bit numerical warmup precedes the explicit shared allowance; the larger precision floor retains conservative field-degree proofs when the 4096-bit dependency search declines. Independent rational oracles check both approximations; every definite sign must agree, and an unlimited retry must certify and retain the result at zero budget. This is a scoped accounting/certificate replay, not a wall-time or memory proof.

Each definitive sign agrees with the exact identity; unlimited retry certifies it and a later zero-budget query retains the proof. Python Fraction and Rug independently check each numerical observation against the exact rational perturbation. A finite public/serialized corpus, not an allocation/time proof.

decision: After independent existence checks, retained upper bounds prove strict unit-range membership and retained positive exact binades prove x >= 1 before coefficient recognition. Keep the measured completeness gain: 52 previously exhausting private proof queries and 38 additional public query schedules complete at unchanged allowances. All prior successful samples and definite signs remain. This implements the accepted strengthening-only cache rule; main admission stays separate.
limits: The new nine test bodies were frozen against the retained v1672 runtime before implementation. The three expected baseline proof-order failures remain archived. Private raw-wrapper diagnostics and their internal lower-bound existence preparation are not public API coverage.

The public domain survey explicitly prewarms pi; other global constants evolve in its frozen process order. Its 1584 queries, 36 fine retries and 144 zero-work cached queries use independent directed numerical enclosures, without a globally cold-process claim.

The original fixed-CPU comparison stopped on the retained v1672 baseline SIGXCPU after 864 successful processes. The interrupted stage is unknown. The equal larger-cap algebraic diagnostic does not pass or replace that failure; the earlier v1638 baseline failure also remains preserved.

Cost evidence comprises 1602 successful processes, one failed baseline process and 1135 separate CPU preparations. The sole initial above-five-percent increase changes from 8.37 to 2.45 percent in the predeclared 27-pair repeat; keep both observations. No uniform speedup is claimed, and the older v1672 integer tradeoff remains retained.

Public domain-query consumption decreases in 396 rows and increases in eight; 434 allocation observations change as more evaluation becomes reachable. The zero-allocation claim applies only to the 56 focused private proof queries. EvaluationBudget excludes bytes, time and unmetered algebraic helpers.

The 78 private-kernel replay cases check result shapes. The 4129-case total is not a count of independent numerical oracle checks. The separate 1584-case retained replay comparison changes only sixteen accounting fields, all eight consumption rows decreasing by six.

Full-stack tests retain 33 ignored tests and fourteen unchanged Cargo example-filename warnings. Both strict Clippy configurations pass without warnings. The checks cover the recorded five-crate stack, not every CI job or full-board admission.
The prior log-range warmup comment is corrected without changing any setup, expression, order or assertion. All previously archived source snapshots remain immutable.

All 44 prior conditional proof and guard inputs remain unchanged. No fresh Verus run is claimed. The new cached-bound helper and runtime domain traversal are outside that proof target; all thirteen whole-crate obligation groups remain open.

Main retains its original scalar failure and all 49 preexisting worktree entries. Native combination, whole-board admission, all 39 properties, 14 targets and crate future work remain open. No push occurred.
